author: Chantal Eco
title: Envi advocates oppose Gemini Wind Project in Samar
content:
Environmental advocates and students from Christ the King College and Northwest Samar State University in Calbayog City, Samar held a peace rally on Monday, August 3, to call for the review of Vena Energy’s Gemini Wind Power Project.

The turbines were originally planned inside the Calbayog Pan-as Hayiban Protected Landscape (CPHPL). After opposition to building within it, Vena Energy agreed to reapply for a new Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) and moved the site. But advocates later learned that at least three turbines will still rise upstream of Tarangban Falls, a popular destination in a city known as the “City of Waterfalls.” (Video report by Chantal Eco)

The post Envi advocates oppose Gemini Wind Project in Samar appeared first on Bulatlat.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: People’s SONA 2026 | Filipinos in New Zealand call for end to ‘exploitative visa system,’ jobs in PH
content:
Filipinos gathered in Britomart, Auckland as Ferdinand Marcos Jr. delivered his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) in the Philippines, July 27.

Organized by Bayan, Migrante, Anakbayan and Gabriela, the protest highlighted the demands of overseas Filipino workers in New Zealand.

“We have seen migrant workers afraid to report exploitation because their visas tie them to their employers. We have seen wage theft. We have seen excessive working hours. We have seen workers treated as though they are temporary commodities instead of human beings,” Gabriela Aotearoa said in a statement.

They underscored that the exploitation of migrant labor in Aotearoa is connected to the economic conditions that force many Filipinos to leave the country. “When decent work disappears in one country, exploitation appears in another. That is why international solidarity matters. Because our struggles are interconnected,” Gabriela Aotearoa added.

They reiterated their demand for the Philippine government to create quality jobs and undertake genuine development of the economy.

Photos courtesy of Migrante Aotearoa

title: Recognized, but not prioritized? LGBTQIA+ rights absent from past Marcos SONAs
content:
Kath Rabang working on an art project. Photo courtesy of Kath Rabang.

“Recognition is not enough without concrete rights.”

By Kasheena Camacho Bulatlat.com

Related story: We all deserve to bask in sunshine

MANILA — Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has publicly recognized the LGBTQIA+ community through Executive Order No. 51, annual Pride Month statements, and meetings with LGBTQIA+ organizations since taking office in 2022. But a review of his four State of the Nation Addresses (SONA) found no explicit mention of LGBTQIA+ rights, the proposed Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC) Equality Bill, or other national legislative measures protecting LGBTQIA+ Filipinos.

The absence of LGBTQIA+ rights from four consecutive SONAs comes despite executive initiatives recognizing the community and years-long calls from advocates to enact a national anti-discrimination legislation.

For some LGBTQIA+ Filipinos, the gap between public recognition and legal protection is reflected not in policy documents but in their everyday interactions with schools, workplaces, hospitals, and even their own families.

For Cleothena (not her real name), a transgender woman employed at a government agency who requested anonymity for fear of workplace repercussions, that gap became apparent only weeks after she started working.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: We all deserve to bask in sunshine
content:
Vince and Mac are attending LoveLaban 2026 at the University of the Philippines. Photo courtesy of Vince Mangulabnan.

After eight years together, one LGBTQIA+ couple discovered that the law still did not recognize their relationship when it mattered most, exposing the legal gaps that continue to leave same-sex partners unprotected.

By Kasheena Camacho Bulatlat.com

MANILA — When Vince’s partner, Mac, underwent surgery earlier this year, hospital staff asked for a legally recognized next of kin to authorize medical decisions if complications arise. Despite eight years together, Vince could not fill that role because Philippine law does not recognize their relationship, exposing a legal gap that leaves many long-term LGBTQIA+ couples without legal standing in medical emergencies.

Hospital staff accommodated Vince whenever they could, but institutional procedures still followed existing law. If Mac had become unable to make medical decisions, that authority would have gone to a legally recognized family member—not to the person who had shared his life for eight years

“I was hurt. I was angry at the system. I felt helpless,” Vince said. “At that moment, it felt like our relationship was being invalidated. author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: ‘Government, businesses use renewable energy projects to exploit resources’
content:
Indigenous peoples, farmers, and environmental rights advocates conducted a “pagsisibat” symbolic action in rejection of destructive renewable energy projects in a July 21 forum at the Commission of Human Rights, Quezon City. Photo by Elisha Beatrice Umali

“Marcos Jr. has a big role in the currently existing environmental plunder.”

By Elisha Beatrice Umali Bulatlat.com

MANILA — The country’s expansion of renewable energy (RE) sources places Filipino indigenous peoples (IP) groups, farmers, fisherfolk, and the urban poor at the forefront of environmental and human rights violations, health hazards, displacement and loss of livelihood.

Under the Philippine Energy Plan (2023-2050), the government aims for a 50% RE share in the country’s power generation mix by 2040 and a larger percent of RE in energy sourcing by 2050.

As of 2026, the country is still reliant on fossil fuels such as coal (56.4%) and gas (17.9%) for its energy supply. A 2025 report by the Philippine Center of Investigative Journalism showed that these “dirty” energy generation remains dominated by the Aboitiz, Ang, and Lopez families.

Cathleen de Guzman of Kalikasan People’s Network for the Environment asked, “Who are the ones actually benefitting from these renewable energy projects?”

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Media community faces killings, weaponization of laws under Marcos Jr.
content:
A placard highlighting a call to stop the attacks against community journalists placed on the floor during a protest action at the UP College of Media and Communication on May 2, 2025, a day before World Press Freedom Day. Photo by Alex Culla/Bulatlat

“Protecting press freedom is a shared responsibility. Without it, the public’s right to know and the foundations of democratic society are at risk.”

CAGAYAN DE ORO — Four years since Ferdinand Marcos Jr. assumed the presidency, press freedom violations continue.

Eleven journalists and media workers were killed under his administration, according to the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP), although two of them were initially reported as not work-related. The latest case happened in May when Nestor Micator , radio broadcaster of D’Empire Radio, was shot dead by an unidentified assailant in Malidegao town which is under the Special Geographic Area of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

Community journalist RJ Nichole Ledesma was also killed during a military operation in Toboso, Negros Occidental, in April. He was reportedly in the area doing community work. However, the Philippine Army stressed that he was a New People’s Army (NPA) combatant, a claim assailed by media and human rights organizations.

title: Filipino children still oppressed under Marcos Jr. admin
content:
Child rights advocates hold puzzle pieces and break a chain, as part of their symbolic action after a July 23 forum at the Commission of Human Rights, Quezon City ahead of Marcos Jr.’s 2026 SONA. Photo by Elisha Beatrice Umali

“Instead of lowering [the minimum age of criminal responsibility], the government must ensure first that our children and youth are growing up in a safe environment, whether inside their homes, schools, and in the community.”

By Elisha Beatrice Umali Bulatlat.com

MANILA — The longstanding problems of a Filipino child continue to persist under the Marcos Jr. administration.

Different child rights organizations cited poverty, faulty basic education systems, lagging early childhood care and development (EECD), stunting and malnutrition, as well as systemic rights abuses as main issues children face in the country.

“Nine percent of Filipino children come from the working class and farmers that experience extreme poverty. This means that a child’s life is not separate from the lived realities of their families,” said Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns spokesperson m Elle Buntag.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Resolve the continuing Marawi displacement, Marcos Jr. urged
content:
Marawi war-displaced families and several organizations stage a protest action on May 23, 2026, in Marawi City in commemoration of the ninth year of the Marawi Siege, demanding their kambalingan (safe and dignified return). Photo from the Reclaiming Marawi Movement.

The prolonged and permanent displacement, long-overdue monetary compensation, and the dire situation of displaced families reflect “the true face of Marawi’s rehabilitation.”

CAGAYAN DE ORO — Ferdinand Marcos Jr. did not mention anything about Marawi rehabilitation during his State of the Nation Address (SONA) last year. Now, families displaced by the Marawi Siege in 2017 urged the current administration to put an end to their continuing displacement.

The Reclaiming Marawi Movement (RMM), a group led by internally displaced persons (IDPs) demanding for their immediate return, called on the Marcos Jr. administration to fast-track the release of the monetary compensation, which property owners are entitled to under the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act.

Many claimants have used their compensation for house repair, as reflected in a study conducted last year by the Marawi Compensation Board (MCB), the government body that awards monetary compensation.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Media groups decry harassment of journalists, activist during protest
content:
Protesters face police personnel during the protest action in connection with the visit of United States State Secretary Marco Rubio in the country for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Pasay City on July 22, 2026. Photo courtesy of Altermidya

“Any act by law enforcement that prevents members of the press from documenting public assemblies undermines press freedom.”

CAGAYAN DE ORO — Several media organizations denounced the police harassment of photojournalists and an activist during a public demonstration in Pasay City on Wednesday, July 22.

In a statement, the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) said members of the Southern Police District allegedly arrested environmental activist and Bulatlat contributor Jian Sanz while taking photos during a mobilization in connection with the visit of United States State Secretary Marco Rubio in the country for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

Sanz said that the police prevented three women who were part of a paralegal team from entering the police station. However, lawyer Maria Sol Taule of the human rights alliance Karapatan came to her aid. Sanz was released after being detained for about 40 minutes.

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: UN expert questions handling of rights defender killed by police
content:
UN Special Rapporteur on human rights defender Mary Lawlor urged the Philippine government to reopen the investigation, stressing that the documentary evidence tends to support wrongful death litigation.

MANILA — The killing of labor organizer Jude Thaddeus Fernandez was cited by former United Nations Special Rapporteur on human rights defender Mary Lawlor in her report released on July 14.

“The Philippine National Police (PNP)’s failure to properly investigate the circumstances of Jude’s killing is evident in its shoddy and possibly wilfully poor investigative practice and through its conflicted and falsifiable narrative around the victim’s identity,” the report noted.

Fernandez was killed on September 29, 2023 by elements of the Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG). He joined the Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) in 1989.

State forces claimed that Fernandez fought back (nanlaban), a common narrative to justify extrajudicial killings in the Philippines. However, independent fact-finding led by KMU, human rights organizations, and progressive lawmakers found that there were “no signs of resistance on the part of Fernandez when he was gunned down.”

title: Mining firm files cyberlibel vs anti-mining residents’ lawyer
content:
Indigenous Peoples, and environmental groups protested in front of the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) and the Department of Environment and National Resources (DENR) after the recent mining exploration activities of North Luzon Mineral Resource Corporation (NLMRC) in Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya. (Photo by Viggo Sarmago/Bulatlat)

The cyberlibel complaint against Santos comes amid continuing opposition to NLMRC’s exploration activities, with residents maintaining a barricade to protest the company’s operations.

MANILA — A lawyer representing anti-mining residents in Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya faces a cyberlibel complaint from mining firm North Luzon Mineral Resources Corporation (NLMRC) over his criticism of the company’s exploration activities.

The complaint dated July 2 stemmed from a Facebook video in which lawyer Fidel Santos allegedly suggested that NLMRC “failed to comply with mandatory legal processes” in obtaining an exploration permit.

The exploration permit covers 4,456 hectares of land which residents stressed is part of their ancestral domain and a source of livelihood.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Lawmakers urged to investigate Meralco over dubious electricity rates
content:
Biggest electric distributor firm Meralco has a record of overcharging consumers and entering into questionable supply deals with sister companies. (File Photo by Bulatlat)

“Congress should investigate why Meralco was not held accountable and how laws could be strengthened to truly defend the rights of the people.”

MANILA – The Makabayan bloc urged the House Committee on Energy on July 13 to investigate Meralco after receiving complaints of alleged incorrect meter readings and unusually high electricity rates.

The effects of the US-Israel attacks on Iran affected local electricity rates, with Meralco citing oil price hikes as a factor in their monthly residential rate increase. Electricity rates surged a total of P1.876 per kilowatt-hour in seven months, surpassing a whole year’s increase of P1.21 in 2025.

However, complaints gathered from social media and from Gabriela’s personal account showed that monthly bills doubled or tripled despite unchanged consumption patterns.

Comparing price hikes between January and July 2026, the supposed increase for a household with an average consumption of 200 kWh was P375.

Gabriela Women’s Party Rep. Sarah Elago said that this incident uncovers the Energy Regulatory Commission’s (ERC) failure to protect consumers from dubious billings.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Groups condemn illegal assembly charges vs activists
content:
Progressive groups protest outside a court in Manila where four mass leaders are facing illegal assembly charges. (Photo by Mayo Lorengal/Bulatlat)

“It’s infuriating that those who are protesting to demand for a daily living wage of P1,200 ($19.53), lower prices of basic goods, and respect for the rights of workers and ordinary Filipinos are the very ones being charged.”

Progressive groups protested the illegal assembly case filed against four activist leaders, warning that the charges threaten Filipinos’ constitutional right to peaceful assembly and protest.

They were charged with violating Section 13, Paragraph A of Batas Pambansa (BP) 880 (Public Assembly Act) for allegedly holding a public assembly without a permit. July 14 was the scheduled arraignment of the four leaders.

In a statement, the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) condemned the filing of charges against its president Renato Reyes Jr. and secretary general Mong Palatino, as well as Kilusang Mayo Uno Chairperson Jerome Adonis and PISTON Chairperson Mody Floranda, over the Labor Day protest on May 1.

Bayan said that the case is the first in nearly two decades in which a charge under BP 880 has proceeded to a court trial. The alliance warned that the prosecution could set a dangerous precedent by using the law against protest leaders and government critics.

author: Maverick Avila
title: US marine biologist killed in Negros
content:
Dr. Kent Carpenter produced research that reshaped how scientists understand marine life in the Philippines.

BANGKOK, Thailand – A US marine biologist was shot to death at his residence on the night of July 12, 2026, Sunday, in Sibulan, Negros.

Dr. Kent Carpenter was also a professor and expert witness for the Philippines in its arbitration case against China over the South China Sea. He studied the Philippine marine fisheries for more than five decades.

On the night of his killing, three unidentified male suspects, wearing bonnets, reportedly entered the residence of Carpenter.

Carpenter was a research associate at Silliman University (SU) and professor emeritus of biological sciences at the Old Dominion University in Virginia, USA. Starting 1976, he collaborated with the university along with the late National Scientist Dr. Angel C. Alcala and fellow marine scientists in pioneering studies on the Philippines’ rich marine ecosystems.

“Through their partnership helped establish SU as an internationally respected center for marine and coastal research and contributed significantly to the scientific understanding of coral reef biodiversity, reef fish ecology, fisheries sustainability, and marine conservation,” the official statement of the Silliman University reads.

Carpenter produced research that reshaped how scientists understand marine life in the Philippines.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Indigenous Peoples, environmentalists demand cancellation of Nueva Vizcaya mining permit
content:
MANILA – Indigenous Peoples and environmental groups trooped to the offices of the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) on Tuesday, July 14 following the recent mining exploration activities of the North Luzon Mineral Resource Corporation (NLMRC) in Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya.

The community set up a barricade last May 8, 2026 in barangay Pao, Kasibu to halt the 4,456 hectare mining exploration project of NLMRC who dubiously obtained an exploration permit last year. The community pushed back and asserted their right to land and filed a cancellation of its permit with the MGB to permanently stop its operations.

Communities in Nueva Vizcaya are no strangers to foreign companies seeking to extract critical minerals, such as copper and gold. Community members shared that the NLMRC have begun trenching operations in the area, infringing on the Indigenous Peoples right to free, prior and informed consent. They also pointed out that they are still affected by the Didipio Gold-Copper Project, which poisoned their rivers and displaced livelihoods.

The Alyansa ng Novo Vizcayano para sa Kalikasan also condemned Canadian-Based OceanaGold’s planned $1.9B investment to expand and extend the operations of the Didipio Gold-Copper Project until 2037.
